title: Bounding the Graph Capacity with Quantum Mechanics and Finite Automata
text:
The Shannon capacity \Theta of a graph G measures the zero-error capacity of a communication channel with symbols V(G) and a confusion graph G. Denote by \alpha(G) the size of the largest independent set in G, and by \boxtimes the strong graph product. G^{\boxtimes n} is the n -fold strong graph product of G with itself. Then the Shannon capacity is defined [1] as

The limit always exists, as a consequence of Fekete’s Lemma and the supermultiplicativity of \alpha. In terms of communication, \Theta(G) counts asymptotically how many n -character strings with symbols in V(G) can be all pairwise distinguishable: for any pair of strings x and y, there is at least one position x_{i} and y_{i} that is not confusable, i.e. (x_{i},y_{i})\not\in E(G).

The behavior of the Shannon capacity is difficult to control [2,3,4]. While every independent set of a G^{\boxtimes n} yields a lower bound, and these lower bounds converge, it is difficult to identify when the sequence might converge [3]. While it is true that

as one would expect, equality does not hold in general [2,5]. The Shannon capacity of the 5-cycle, \Theta(C_{5})\geq\sqrt{\alpha(G^{\boxtimes 2})}=\sqrt{5}, was open for 24 years until Lovasz [6] provided a matching upper bound of \sqrt{5}, a bound that today is often understood in terms of semidefinite programming. Other upper bound techniques [7,8] have appeared, but even the capacity of the 7-cycle remains open. Recently, Bi & Tang [4] showed that a large class of upper bounds based on conic programming cannot beat the bound of Lovasz. It is not even known whether graph capacity is computable.

In this paper we put forward a new upper bound on Shannon capacity using a Sum of Squares hierarchy. We start by relating Shannon capacity to what we call the reversible capacity of a graph. This quantity comes from a perspective less of graph theory, and more returning to the original setting of communication channels and error correcting languages: in particular, languages recognized by reversible DFAs [9,10]. We show that reversible capacity converges to the Shannon capacity in a controlled way, so that if the reversible capacity is computable, then the Shannon capacity is too (Theorem 11). Motivated by this, a further modification as the unitary capacity is equal to the Shannon capacity, and can be written as a tensor product Noncommutative Polynomial Optimization (NPO) problem [11,12]. This problem has convergent upper bounds to the commuting operator value, which is an upper bound to the true value that we conjecture to be tight.

If the conjecture is proved correct and our NPO has equal commuting operator and tensor product values, then this would give a computable algorithm for the zero-erro capacity of a graph.
